newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mercedes moves spark slim share reaction.
newsitem.headline: Mercedes moves spark slim share reaction.

text.p: The resignation of Mercedes chief executive Helmut Werner on Thursday should have little impact on the shares of parent group Daimler-Benz AG, German share market traders said on Thursday.

Werner resigned after a prolonged struggle over reshaping the industrial group. Daimler chief executive Juergen Schrempp had pushed for Mercedes to be folded into the overall Daimler structure and not remain an independent group.
Traders said the anticipated moves at Daimler, which had been discussed in markets for the last few weeks, were already priced into Daimler's shares.

"The resignation of Werner is no big surprise. It was clear that Schrempp would win in this restructuring. But the question is where is Werner going to go," said Josh Waiblinger at BHF Bank in Frankfurt.
Added another trader: "Werner's resignation has pretty much been priced into the market."
Daimler shares were down 60 pfennigs at 115.10 marks ($72.46) in post-bourse IBIS DAX electronic dealings after ending the bourse session down 1.30 marks at 115.60 marks.
Daimler shares had been under pressure earlier on Thursday due to rumours -- which were denied by Daimler -- that it was planning an upcoming rights issue.
In addition, Daimler shares have been trading near record highs, prompting some bouts of profit-taking, traders said.
